question: A newsletter team produces about thirty short social posts each week and a person edits every one before it goes out. Which tier fits this work best?
options: A) A different tier for each post, chosen according to which social platform it is destined for.
B) The fastest and cheapest tier, since the posts are short, routine and edited by a person after.
C) The deepest-reasoning tier, because published content should always use the very strongest option.
D) The default middle tier, because short marketing copy is too nuanced for any lighter option.
correct_answers: B) The fastest and cheapest tier, since the posts are short, routine and edited by a person after.
explanations: Incorrect. The platform does not change the reasoning the task requires, so varying tier by channel is arbitrary.
Correct. High volume, low complexity and a human editing step is exactly the profile the fastest tier is for; reasoning depth would add little to a two-line post.
Incorrect. The posts are short and human-edited, so the extra depth changes little while consuming much more allowance.
Incorrect. It would work, but it spends more allowance than thirty short, edited posts a week justify.
